facts.statement: Sclerocormus lived during the Early Triassic period.
facts.quote: Sclerocormus is an extinct genus of ichthyosauriform from the early Triassic period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sclerocormus were discovered in central Anhui Province, China.
facts.quote: The fossil was discovered in the central Anhui Province, China.

facts.statement: Sclerocormus is known from only one mostly complete fossil specimen.
facts.quote: It is currently only known from one specimen, however the fossil is mostly complete

facts.statement: This specimen provides significant insight into the early evolution of ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: further increases the understanding of the early evolution of ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Sclerocormus measured about 1.6 meters in length and weighed more than 15 kilograms.
facts.quote: Sclerocormus is much larger than its closest relative Cartorhynchus, with a total body length of 1.6 m and body mass of more than 15 kg.

facts.statement: The skull of Sclerocormus was unusually short, making up only 6.25% of its total body length.
facts.quote: The skull is unusually short at only 6.25% of its body length, compared to 12% in Chaohusaurus and 15% in Hupehsuchus.

facts.statement: The nasal bones of Sclerocormus extended all the way to the tip of its snout.
facts.quote: Unusually, the nasals of Sclerocormus extend to the tip of the snout, a trait which it shares with Cartorhynchus.

facts.statement: Large upper temporal fenestrae in Sclerocormus suggest it may have had a strong bite force despite having no teeth.
facts.quote: The upper temporal fenestrae are large, possibly indicating a strong bite force despite its lack of teeth.

facts.statement: Sclerocormus had a short, heavily built trunk with broad, flattened ribs.
facts.quote: The trunk is short and heavily built, with broad and flattened ribs.

facts.statement: Sclerocormus possessed an extensive gastral rib basket running along its underside in two parallel series.
facts.quote: An extensive gastral rib basket runs along the underside in two parallel series on each side.

facts.statement: The tail of Sclerocormus was very long and slender, made of at least 67 vertebrae, and lacked a fluke.
facts.quote: The tail itself is very long and slender, composed of at least 67 caudal vertebrae, and does not appear to have had a fluke.

facts.statement: Small dermal ossicles measuring 2–5 mm were found on the neck of Sclerocormus, resembling pelvic ossicles of saurosphargids.
facts.quote: Small dermal ossicles were reported from the cervical region, ranging in size between 2–5 mm, and curiously resemble the pelvic ossicles of saurosphargids.

facts.statement: The name Sclerocormus parviceps means 'stiff trunk' and 'small skull' in Greek and Latin.
facts.quote: The full binomial name, Sclerocormus parviceps, comes from the Greek words for 'stiff trunk' (σκληρός, skleros and κορμός, kormos) and the Latin words for 'small skull' (parvus and caput).

facts.statement: Jiang et al. (2016) classified Sclerocormus as a basal ichthyosauriform and a sister taxon to Cartorhynchus.
facts.quote: In the phylogenetic analysis performed by Jiang et al. (2016), Sclerocormus was found to be a basal ichthyosaurform and a sister taxon to Cartorhynchus.

facts.statement: Later research determined that the clade Nasorostra is synonymous with the family Omphalosauridae.
facts.quote: Later work revealed that the clade Nasorostra is synonymous with the earlier-named Omphalosauridae, as Omphalosaurus share more features with these Chinese taxa than previously recognized.

facts.statement: Sclerocormus likely lived in shallow waters and was probably a slow swimmer due to its heavy build.
facts.quote: Due to its heavy build and body shape, Sclerocormus likely inhabited shallow waters, as with Cartorhynchus, and was probably a slow swimmer.

facts.statement: Sclerocormus was likely a suction feeder that used its narrow, toothless snout to suck in soft-bodied prey.
facts.quote: The narrow, toothless snout indicates Sclerocormus was likely a suction feeder, using its snout to generate syringe-like pressure concentration to suck in soft-bodied prey.

facts.statement: Sclerocormus could only feed on prey much smaller than itself due to its small jaws and head.
facts.quote: Due to the small size of its jaws and head relative to its body, Sclerocormus would have been limited to feeding on prey much smaller than itself.

facts.statement: It was debated whether Sclerocormus was simply a large or mature version of Cartorhynchus before anatomical differences were confirmed.
facts.quote: As the holotype of Cartorhynchus was potentially not fully mature, it was possible Sclerocormus simply represented a large or mature Cartorhynchus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Sclerocormus likely inhabited shallow waters and was probably a slow swimmer due to its heavy build and body shape.
facts.quote: Debido a su constitución pesada y su forma corporal, es probable que Sclerocormus habitara aguas poco profundas, como ocurre con Cartorhynchus, y sería probablemente un nadador lento.

facts.statement: Its narrow, toothless snout suggests Sclerocormus likely fed by suction, using its snout to generate pressure like a syringe to suck in soft-bodied prey.
facts.quote: El hocico estrecho y desdentado indica que Sclerocormus posiblemente se alimentaba por medio de la succión, usando su hocico para generar concentración de presión como una jeringa, que terminaba por succionar a las presas de cuerpo blando.

facts.statement: Given the small size of its jaws and head relative to its body, Sclerocormus was likely limited to eating prey much smaller than itself.
facts.quote: Considerando el pequeño tamaño de las mandíbulas y de la cabeza en relación con el cuerpo, Sclerocormus debió haberse limitado a devorar presas mucho menores que él mismo.

facts.statement: A 2016 phylogenetic analysis by Jiang et al. found that Sclerocormus was a basal ichthyosauriform and the sister taxon to Cartorhynchus.
facts.quote: En el análisis filogenético realizado por Jiang et al. 2016, se encontró que Sclerocormus era un ictiosauriforme basal y el taxón hermano de Cartorhynchus.

facts.statement: Jiang et al. erected the new clade Nasorostra ("nose beak") for these two genera, which itself is a sister taxon to Ichthyopterygia.
facts.quote: Jiang et al. erigieron el nuevo clado Nasorostra ("nariz pico") para estos dos géneros, que en sí mismo es un taxón hermano de Ichthyopterygia.

facts.statement: It was initially hypothesized that Sclerocormus might simply represent a large or mature Cartorhynchus, since the holotype of Cartorhynchus could be an immature individual.
facts.quote: Ya que el espécimen holotipo de Cartorhynchus es potencialmente un individuo aún no completamente desarrollado, sería posible que Sclerocormus simplemente representara a un Cartorhynchus grande o maduro.

facts.statement: However, it was determined that Sclerocormus is distinct from Cartorhynchus due to significant anatomical differences, including different numbers of presacral vertebrae and gastralia shape.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, se estableció que ese no es el caso, ya que hay diferencias anatómicas significativas entre ambos géneros, incluyendo números diferentes de vértebras presacrales y la forma de la gastralia, que pueden distinguir a ambos taxones.

facts.statement: The parent group of Sclerocormus is Omphalosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Omphalosauridae

facts.statement: Sclerocormus belongs to the family Omphalosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Omphalosauridae

facts.statement: Sclerocormus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Sclerocormus is Sclerocormus parviceps.
facts.quote: Type species: Sclerocormus parviceps

facts.statement: There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of Sclerocormus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

rejected.statement: Sclerocormus had unusual proportions including a short heavy trunk, a very long tail over 92 cm (58% of body length), and a small skull with a short, narrow, toothless snout.
rejected.quote: Its proportions were unusual amongst basal ichthyosauriformes, with a short, heavily built trunk, a very long tail over 92 cm long (58% of the total body length), and a small skull with a short, narrow snout and toothless jaws.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'trunk a very long tail over 92 cm'

rejected.statement: Jiang et al. (2016) created the clade Nasorostra to group Sclerocormus and Cartorhynchus together.
rejected.quote: Jiang et al. erected the new clade Nasorostra ('nose beak') for these two taxa, itself a sister taxon to Ichthyopterygia.
